newsitem.title: GERMANY: BWM seeks higher return on sales-interview.
newsitem.headline: BWM seeks higher return on sales-interview.

text.p: German carmaker BMW AG intends to have a seven percent pre-tax return on sales within the next 10 years on a groupwide basis, BMW chief executive Bernd Pischetsrieder said in an interview on Saturday.

Pischetsrieder told the Boersen Zeitung that the goal was not only for BMW's carmaker division, which had a 1996 pre-tax return on sales of 6.4 percent, but also included the Rover carmaker unit in Britain and BMW's aircraft engine venture.
But he also said the strong pound may endanger BMW's goal of turning a profit at Rover by the year 2000 if the British currency remains strong for some time.
Pischetsrieder, however, said the weaker mark was helping to boost BMW's foreign sales. The sale this year of about 60,000 BMW vehicles in the U.K. would also help offset the strong pound, he said.
BMW also does not plan any capital raising measures in the near-term and would finance expansion from within.
He said demand for BMW vehicles was particularly strong in Asia, above all in Japan where the carmaker sold 36,300 vehicles in 1996.
